description_ru: GLACIERS AND GLACIERETTES: ice, firn and snow; stagnant ice caps and cliff glaciers
note: GSC Map 1753A Western Melville Island (Hodgson 1992), UTM, raster scan; swatch sampled by hand

description_ru: COLLUVIAL DEPOSITS: silty clay to rubble diamicton derived from upslope deposits; 1-5 m; mainly weathered rock incorporating till and marine or deltaic deposits
FLUVIAL deposits, active: 1-3 m; subject to flooding during snowmelt freshet
FLUVIAL deposits, inactive: 1-20 m; terraces and abandoned segments of deltas and fans
note: swatch sampled by hand (very pale cream; missed by the finder)

description_ru: MARINE: raised beaches: sand, minor silt or gravel; 1-2 m; single ridges or flights of emerged low amplitude ridges
MARINE: emerged neritic deposits: silt and fine sand, scattered ice-rafted clasts; 1-6 m
GLACIOLACUSTRINE OR EMERGED GLACIOMARINE DEPOSITS: silt and fine sand, rare dropstones; rhythmic bedding; 1-20 m
note: legend does not separate glaciolacustrine from glaciomarine

description_ru: GLACIOFLUVIAL: outwash: ice contact sediments and valley train deltas; boulder to granule gravel over sand or silt; up to 20 m
GLACIOFLUVIAL: kames and eskers: boulder to granule gravel and silty sand; 2-20 m
MORAINAL: till, Laurentide: granule to boulder clasts in calcareous silty matrix; 5-20 m; flat to ridged
MORAINAL: till, local provenance: clasts of quartzitic sandstone in silty sand matrix; 1-10 m; 2a' = till veneer
WEATHERED BEDROCK: rubble: angular to subround blocks in sand or silt matrix; tablelands, ridges, scarps
WEATHERED BEDROCK: sand: discontinuous lag gravel veneer, minor rubble or silty sand, from friable sandstone and siltstone
WEATHERED BEDROCK: rubble to fines, undivided
WEATHERED BEDROCK: fines: fine sand, silt, minor clay; derived from weak lithologies; rolling lowlands
